text_blocks.snippet: Steps to Take After a Denial

list.snippet: Read the written denial: Ask for a detailed written explanation pointing to specific policy language or inspection findings (such as "wear and tear," "cosmetic damage," or storm dates outside the policy window).
Review your policy: Check your deductible, whether you have Replacement Cost Value (RCV) or Actual Cash Value (ACV), and any exclusions or limits for wind, hail, or roof age.
Document everything: Save all emails, letters, and call notes. Take clear photos and videos of exterior roof damage and any interior leak signs, plus save local weather records from the storm date.

Get an independent inspection: Hire a reputable local roofing contractor to inspect every slope and write a technical report with photos and measurements. Having a knowledgeable roofer on-site can help spot missed damage.

Request a reinspection or appeal: Submit your new evidence and ask the insurer for a reinspection, reconsideration, or formal appeal. If the claim was partially approved or underpaid, your roofer may also submit a supplement for missed items or code upgrades.
Escalate if needed: If disputes persist, you can consider a licensed public adjuster, a property insurance attorney, or filing a complaint with your state department of insurance.
